input.question: The human bodies needs 20 amino acids, 10 are essential; are there other common animals or plants that use different amino acids? Is there a theoretical limit to the amount of amino acids possible?
input.ground_truth: Amino acids can be post-translationally be modified, so there is a large variety in that area. Also, the 21 (not 20) "standard" amino acids are commonly found in eukaryotes. Prokaryotes (bacteria and such) also have other amino acids like selocysteine and pyrrolysine.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: The human bodies needs 20 amino acids, 10 are essential; are there other common animals or plants that use different amino acids? Is there a theoretical limit to the amount of amino acids possible?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s make this super simple!

Imagine your body is like a big LEGO set, and the LEGO bricks are like amino acids. Your body needs 20 special LEGO bricks (amino acids) to build everything. But, you can only get 10 of those special bricks from your food—you can’t make them yourself, so you *need* to eat them. The other 10 you can make by yourself, like if you had some extra LEGO bricks at home and could build the rest.

Now, other animals, like cats or birds, also need some special LEGO bricks (amino acids) from their food, but sometimes they need different ones or different amounts than humans.

Plants are a little different! They can make all their own LEGO bricks (amino acids) because they have a special way to build them using sunlight.

About the “theoretical limit”—imagine if there were a million different LEGO bricks, not just 20. In theory, maybe there *could* be more kinds of bricks, but for living things on Earth, 20 is what we use. Scientists think 20 is enough for all the things our bodies need to build. But maybe on another planet, a different creature could use more or different kinds of bricks!

So, different living things use different LEGO bricks (amino acids), and on Earth, 20 is the number we use, but maybe not everywhere in the universe!
